subject: Kube gateway & node-fleet storage acceptance for NodeWave POC
messages:
From: Carlos Mendez <carlos.m@nodewave.com>
To: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Cc: Samantha Reed <samantha.reed@nodewave.com>
Date: Fri, 25 Sep 2026 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: NodeWave POC — gateway + node fleet / storage acceptance checklist

Hi Vivek,

Thanks again for the demo last week. NodeWave wants to lock down the acceptance criteria for the on-prem POC so our infra team can provision racks next week. High level asks:

- VPC-ish VLAN mapping (we're doing L2 in the colo) and the gateway pattern you recommend for multi-tenant inference.
- Node fleet definitions (gpu vs cpu, preemptible/burst lanes, eviction priorities).
- Storage behaviour: expected PV types, ephemeral vs persistent, eviction protection for KV caches.

I've attached a rough workbook with our expected workload profile. Can you confirm which items we need to validate during sprint zero and provide a small checklist we can give to our datacenter ops team?

Carlos
Sr. Platform Eng | NodeWave Solutions
attachments: nodewave-workload-profile.xlsx (xlsx)

From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
To: Carlos Mendez <carlos.m@nodewave.com>
Cc: Samantha Reed <samantha.reed@nodewave.com>, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 25 Sep 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: NodeWave POC — gateway + node fleet / storage acceptance checklist

Carlos — thanks, workbook received. Short answer: we can cover everything in a two-day sprint-zero verification split across networking and node/storage validation. Draft acceptance checklist below (I will iterate with Neha and Priyom):

Network & gateway (day 1)
- Confirm VLANs/subnet plan and BGP peering details (if applicable).
- Deploy and validate the egress gateway (NAT + TLS passthrough) with canary traffic.
- Verify route isolation between tenant VLANS (simple L2 isolation + ACL validation).
- Latency smoke test to the nearest region (ping/traceroute + 95th pct)

Node fleet & scheduling (day 2 AM)
- Node classes: gpu-large (A100/80GB), gpu-small (A10), cpu-large (serving), burst-cpu (ephemeral).
- Taints/tolerations and pod priority matrix for preemption behavior.
- KV cache tiers: node-local SSD + cluster-level PVC with ReadWriteMany for larger checkpoints.

Storage & data durability (day 2 PM)
- Validate PV type mapping: fast NVMe for KV and model cache; replicated blockstore for metadata/long-term checkpoints.
- Eviction test: simulate OOM and disk-pressure events; ensure stateful pods either checkpoint or failover according to SLA.
- Backup verification: snapshot policy for PVCs and restore smoke test.

Attachments: I'm dropping a quick topology image and a CSV with initial sizing we used in the demo. Can Neha and Priyom add any additional operational checks we should include?

Next steps:
1) We run that two-day sprint-zero in your staging rack.
2) If green, lock node-classes and storage profiles in the deployment manifest.
3) Hand-off to infra for rack provisioning for production cutover.

Regards,
Vivek Kulkarni
Solutions Engineering | Redwood Inference
attachments: kube-gateway-topology.png (png); storage-sizing-estimates.csv (csv)

From: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
To: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 25 Sep 2026 15:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: NodeWave POC — gateway + node fleet / storage acceptance checklist

Vivek — forwarding with a few edits and ops-level checks. I pulled the sizing into the workbook and added acceptance gates we use for Dedicated onboarding. Key additions:

- Network: we need ACL test vectors (list of IPs/ports) and a failover test for the egress gateway (simulate single DC path failure).
- Node fleet: add GPU driver/hypervisor compatibility check (driver+cuda matrix), container runtime version pinning, and nvme firmware baseline.
- Storage: PV reclaim policy verification, CSI driver perf baseline (iops/latency), and a throttling experiment to confirm QoS.

Operational checklist (short):
1) Precheck: rack inventory, network patching, KVM access validated.
2) Deploy infra: kubeadm/eksd (customer choice), Redwood agent host install and service account validation.
3) Smoke: schedule a simple throughput job that exercises KV cache hot-path and a model inference job to validate end-to-end latency.
4) Failure drills: node reboot, disk failure (unplug test harness), and network partition.

I've attached the updated workbook (sheet: 'ops-checks') and a sample command list we hand to datacenter ops for VLAN patching. Priyom, please add any hardware/gpu affinity constraints we should enforce and the preferred eviction grace periods.

-Neha
Neha Kapoor
Principal SRE | Redwood Inference
attachments: nodewave-acceptance-skeleton.xlsx (xlsx)

From: Carlos Mendez <carlos.m@nodewave.com>
To: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Cc: Samantha Reed <samantha.reed@nodewave.com>
Date: Sat, 26 Sep 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: NodeWave POC — gateway + node fleet / storage acceptance checklist

Vivek / Neha — thanks, this is exactly the level we needed. Confirming NodeWave ops can host the two-day sprint-zero on Oct 4–5 in our staging rack. A couple of clarifications before we schedule:

- For the NVMe tiers: we plan to provide 4 x 3.84TB NVMe per GPU node; is that sufficient for the KV cache working set (your CSV suggests it is, but want to double-check)?
- On egress gateway failover: we have a single external hop now; we'll add a second upstream for the failover test but need the exact handshake steps for BGP or static routes.

I'll schedule the rack access with our colo and loop in our infra lead if you want a short pre-call Monday to confirm ACL test vectors.

Carlos
Sr. Platform Eng | NodeWave Solutions
attachments: none
